newsitem.title: USA: US farmers get first round from $6.4 bln in aid.
newsitem.headline: US farmers get first round from $6.4 bln in aid.

text.p: U.S. farmers will get a first-round payment in the next few weeks out of $6.389 billion in "Freedom to Farm" supports for fiscal 1997, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.

Under the 1996 farm policy law, USDA is required to pay farmers half of their farm subsidies either on December 15 or January 15, at the farmer's option. Final payment must be made by September 30, the end of the fiscal year.
Congress alloted $5.4 billion for payments in fiscal 1997. USDA said the total would swell due to repayments of advance deficiency payments in prior years.
Here is USDA's list of payment rates for the first-round:
Crop-A Alloted by law 1995 returns Total
A-rates are cents per bushel for wheat, corn, sorghum, barley and oats; cents per lb for cotton, dollars per Cwt for rice.
USDA said farmers must submit all paperwork by Thursday if they wanted the first-round payment in December. Paperwork was due by January 15 for the first-round payment to be made that month.
If documentation was not filed by January 15, no first-round payment would be made.
Farmers were required to repay about $1 billion from advance payments on 1995 crops because market prices were so high that, by law, the supports were not needed.
